title: I Used the Screen-Print Station Log on the Intern Who Left My Emulsion

parts.text: I opened station two at 3:12 p.m. and intern Bea had poured my emulsion into a cup labeled leftover. The sheet said: MIX YOUR OWN. WASH THE SCREEN. LOG THE BATCH. I was twenty-seven, member, holding a batch card. Bea shrugged. "Interns are the shop." I photographed the cup, the sheet, and my batch number on her sleeve. Then I asked for the wash log. At 3:19 the studio lead pinged why Bea's name was on my batch. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio lead can see Bea's leftover cup on my batch number in the wash log.

social.video_title: The intern poured my emulsion into a leftover cup — Part 1/2
social.description: Screen-print station, a batch card, an intern's sleeve. I logged the pour. Would you have asked for the wash log?

parts.text: Bea called it salvage until the lead asked for the still. I printed the log, the cup, and the card. The emulsion went back to my mix. Bea washed her own screen and told the next intern salvage was always about optics. Optics is a word interns use when a batch exists. Station policy now has a second line: INTERNS MIX THEIR OWN. I keep my card. Bea brown-bags her jokes. The station finally looks like a sheet, not a cup. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Wash log, returned mix, and a second line. Was salvage ever my batch?
